name: Shoreham Beach
signature: A quiet, unpatrolled Western Port beach — completely off the tourist trail and one of the Peninsula's best kept secrets for a peaceful swim
editorNote:
Shoreham Beach is on the Western Port side of the Peninsula — calmer than Bass Strait, wilder than Port Phillip Bay, and almost entirely off the tourist circuit. The beach is accessed via a short walk through coastal bush and tends to be near-empty even on summer weekends.

The water is calm enough for swimming in normal conditions — Western Port doesn't generate ocean swell — but the tidal movement can be strong and the beach is unpatrolled. Best for experienced ocean swimmers who know how to read water and want somewhere genuinely quiet.

Combine with a hinterland lunch at Montalto or a cellar door visit — Shoreham sits at the eastern end of Red Hill country and is a natural extension of a wine trail day.
whyWeGo: The Peninsula's quietest beach — Western Port, coastal bush, and almost no one else.
ifOnlyOneThing: Arrive mid-morning, swim, walk the beach east toward the rocks, then drive straight to a winery for lunch.
